review_questions_and_results.question: Source Fidelity versus Perceptual Quality
review_questions_and_results.result: Consistent. Fidelity identifies approved/adopted source, matching conditions and intentional differences; image comparisons are diagnostic. Perceptual judgment addresses actual composition, craft and continuous experience.

review_questions_and_results.question: Independent experience validity and expressive completion
review_questions_and_results.result: Consistent. Each retains its own findings; one cannot compensate for the other. Existing design/product integration tracks and authority boundaries remain.

review_questions_and_results.question: Professional-tool artistic freedom
review_questions_and_results.result: Explicit aesthetic goals are project requirements. Task familiarity does not fix navigation geometry, component shape, material or palette.

review_questions_and_results.question: Mature-resource default
review_questions_and_results.result: Page/system/block reuse priority, actual implementation adoption, local trials and evidenced custom-work gaps remain intact. Specialist identity/art production does not exempt generic UI from the reuse default.

review_questions_and_results.question: Repair preserves confirmed direction
review_questions_and_results.result: Concrete reading, operation, composition, motion and runtime defects are repaired at the responsible layer; necessary scope or direction changes remain explicit.

review_questions_and_results.question: Expression in populated core use
review_questions_and_results.result: Review reaches populated navigation, inputs, results, long content, repeated operations and related views.

review_questions_and_results.question: Deterministic and natural-time evidence boundaries
review_questions_and_results.result: Controlled clocks, seeded phases, animation overrides, contact sheets, natural-speed observation and frame-delivery measurements retain distinct claims.

review_questions_and_results.question: Stages and approval burdens
review_questions_and_results.result: init -> iterate -> finish, optional shape and ongoing audit remain. No new compulsory stage, aesthetic score, capture quota, record system or approval checkpoint; established direction and delegation support progress.

review_questions_and_results.question: Compressed deletions and duplication
review_questions_and_results.result: No lost invariant or unnecessary duplication requiring an edit found. Repeated direction-preservation and dual-acceptance instructions are applied at separate planning, craft, integration and verification ownership points.

conclusion.scope: Source-method consistency and frozen/current byte identity only; this is not an output-quality certificate or comparative model evaluation.

limits: No real-user comprehension or usability study

primary_source_research.method: Read primary documentation through web retrieval and authoritative search; distinguish documented claims from methodological inference.
primary_source_research.visual_scope: Primary text only. Two example-image retrieval attempts returned errors; no source image or video was successfully viewed.

sources.name: Pentagram Intrinsic
sources.finding: Generative robotic forms coordinated with typography, graphics, motion and website expression.
sources.boundary: Brand/website case; not work-application usability evidence and no general permission to reuse its assets established.

sources.name: IBM Developer typography
sources.finding: Expressive Plex Mono Light and informative/supportive Plex Sans roles support role-based coherence.
sources.boundary: Exact type choices and brand/language policies are IBM-specific; examples were not visually inspected.

sources.name: Carbon motion
sources.finding: Productive and expressive motion coexist; product teams coordinate motion across components. Page reported update August 12, 2026.
sources.boundary: Its cadence and curves are system choices, not a universal ceiling on an artistic brief. The old /elements/motion/overview URL redirects here.

sources.name: WCAG 2.2 normative motion criteria
sources.finding: 2.2.2 is Level A; 2.3.3 is Level AAA.
sources.boundary: Criteria have specific conditions and essentiality exceptions; a broader project motion practice is distinct from conformance.

sources.name: Understanding WCAG 2.2.2
sources.finding: Automatic moving/blinking/scrolling information exceeding five seconds alongside other content requires applicable control unless essential; automatic updates have no five-second exception.
sources.boundary: Informative explanation of the normative criterion; not a blanket rule about all animation.

sources.name: Understanding WCAG 2.3.3
sources.finding: Nonessential interaction-triggered motion can be disabled; guidance includes controls or reduced-motion preferences.
sources.boundary: Level AAA; do not describe it as an AA requirement.

sources.name: Playwright Clock
sources.finding: Clock control can override timers, animation frames, performance and related sources; fastForward and runFor have different timer behavior.
sources.boundary: Controlled timing supports probes and repeatability, not actual response or frame-delivery measurements.

sources.name: Playwright screenshot animation settings
sources.finding: Disabling screenshot animations can complete finite animations and fire end events, or cancel infinite ones to initial state for capture and resume them afterward.
sources.boundary: Altered captures do not establish natural progression or rhythm.

sources.name: Playwright visual comparisons
sources.finding: Baseline screenshot comparisons depend on rendering environment and configurable pixel tolerances.
sources.boundary: Inference: agreement with a chosen image is distinct from aesthetic success; perceptual quality needs separate review.
